$comment: Read by scripts/ci/detect-stranded-merges.py; validated by its offline tests.
A stranded payload does not become un-stranded because someone decided not to
recover it, so the detector would report it truthfully every Monday forever.
This file is where the decision lives instead, next to the code, so the weekly
tracking issue stays a list of things to do rather than a list of things
already settled -- and so nobody re-litigates a call that was already made.
abandoned        the payload is deliberately not coming back. Silences.
landed-elsewhere the content reached trunk by another route, or the residual
recovering       recovery is in flight. Annotates only -- the finding stays
actionable until the recovery actually lands.
paths: the exact actionable paths the decision covers. A finding whose
actionable set grows beyond this list is reported again, naming the paths the
decision did not cover. Never widen this list without re-adjudicating.
reviewBy (optional): after this date the silence lapses and the finding
returns, so a decision made under time pressure cannot become permanent by

dispositions.reason: The #3055 config-binding fix re-landed on trunk independently and byte-identically; trunk's ConfigurationBindingShapeTests is a superset of the guard #3113 added. Of the two residual paths, AccessPolicy is deliberately left init-only, and Features.Import.Domain.ImportLimits is not IOptions-bound at all (hand-parsed at Honua.Db/Postgres/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs), so init->set there was a no-op and a regression. The real defect behind that path is tracked separately as #3315.

A dual-engine raster capability/cost registry, rejected by name in the ADR-0071 single-engine amendment (epic #3085): all raster GP executes on the isolated GDAL worker and there is no per-job engine selection for the registry to feed. #3091 is closed NOT_PLANNED; the one decision-neutral fragment was re-filed as #3307.
